grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: Defining success before comparing alternatives
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立盲听答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
transcript:
Tutor: What is the primary outcome in your seedling experiment?
Ben: I was going to choose whichever measure shows the largest difference between the lamps.
Tutor: That would make the comparison difficult to interpret. Decide what matters before collecting the final results.
Ben: Then our primary measure will be survival after four weeks. Height will be secondary. A tall seedling that dies is not a success for this project.
Tutor: How will you count survival?
Ben: A plant must have at least one green leaf at the final inspection. We will write that definition in the protocol rather than change it after seeing borderline cases.
Tutor: How many trays?
Ben: Six under each lamp. We will rotate tray positions daily to reduce the effect of being nearest the window.
Tutor: And watering?
Ben: Equal volumes at the same time each morning. The original proposal said water when needed, but different students could interpret that differently.
Tutor: What will you do if a tray is accidentally knocked over?
Ben: Record the accident. We will not silently replace its result. The report will explain whether it was excluded and show how that decision affects the comparison.
Tutor: Good. Send the protocol on Friday, before you start the trial on Monday.

questions.prompt: When will that outcome be inspected?

questions.prompt: Why will tray positions be rotated?
options: To reduce differences caused by window proximity.
To expose only the tallest plants to light.
To remove the need for equal watering.
To prevent any record of lamp assignment.
answers: To reduce differences caused by window proximity.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“reduce the effect of being nearest the window.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: reduce the effect of being nearest the window.

options: Every plant needs exactly the same total water in nature.
The lamps were no longer being compared.
All trays had already been removed.
questions.explanation: 依据原文“different students could interpret that differently.”。正确项保持了原文的范围和关系，其余项改动了该信息。
questions.evidence: different students could interpret that differently.

questions.prompt: How will an accidental tray disturbance be treated?
options: It will automatically prove one lamp ineffective.
It will justify deleting every result.
It will be recorded and its treatment explained.
It will be silently replaced by the best tray.
answers: It will be recorded and its treatment explained.

part1: What do you usually read about this topic?
Have you ever made a choice involving agreeing an outcome before a trial?
What information would help you make that choice?
Who would you ask for a different opinion?
speaking.part2: Describe a decision about agreeing an outcome before a trial. You should say what the decision was, what alternatives were available, what evidence you used, and explain what you would check before recommending it to others.
part3: Why should a primary outcome be selected in advance?
Can a definition still leave borderline cases?
Why might a taller plant not meet a project goal?

transfer.writing: Write an evidence-based paragraph of 120–160 words about agreeing an outcome before a trial. State one claim, support it with a relevant example, acknowledge a limitation, and explain what further evidence would change your conclusion. Use a new example; do not copy the passage.
